questions: Is the cost of swapping P_i and P_{i+1} always exactly i, regardless of the values being swapped, or does it depend on the values (e.g., the larger of the two)?
Can we perform multiple operations simultaneously or only one at a time, and does the order of operations affect the cost calculation (e.g., if indices shift after swaps)?
Does 'sort P in ascending order' mean we must achieve the identity permutation (1,2,...,N), or just any non-decreasing order (allowing duplicates if they existed, but here they don't)?
Are we allowed to choose the same i multiple times in succession, and if so, does the cost accumulate each time?
Is the goal to minimize total cost, and if multiple sequences achieve the sorted order, are we required to find the minimum over all possible sequences?
Does the operation only swap adjacent elements, or are there other allowed operations (like swapping non-adjacent) that might reduce cost?
If N is large (up to 2e5), are there any constraints on time or memory that should influence the algorithm choice, or is any correct algorithm acceptable?
Is the cost i based on the original fixed indices 1..N, or does i refer to the current positions of the elements as we swap them?
